query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: Avg Subcategory Score
per_column.rationale: Aggregates the service subcategory ratings (seat, staff, food, IFE, value). These subjective quality scores plausibly drive the reviewer's recommendation, so this is a candidate cause/driver of the outcome, not a common cause of some other treatment. It is a predictor being attributed, not a confounder.

per_column.name: Value For Money Poor
per_column.rationale: Binary flag derived from the Value For Money rating. It is a candidate cause whose effect on non-recommendation is being attributed. It is not a common cause of any other treatment and the outcome, so it is a treatment/driver, not a confounder.

per_column.name: Overall Rating Band
per_column.rationale: Overall Rating is a summary satisfaction score that sits downstream of the subcategory scores and is essentially co-determined with (a near-proxy of) the recommendation decision. On the path subcategory-scores -> overall-rating -> recommendation it is a mediator/outcome proxy; adjusting for it would bias, not enable, causal attribution.

per_column.name: Weakest Category
per_column.rationale: Identifies which subcategory scored lowest, i.e. names the candidate driver responsible for a poor review. It is a descriptor of the candidate cause, not a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: Non-Rec Risk Factors
per_column.rationale: A post-hoc engineered concatenation of 'poor_X' flags. It mixes candidate causes (poor_value_for_money, poor_seat_comfort, etc.) with 'very_low_overall_rating', which is an outcome proxy/mediator. It is a circular attribution label constructed from outcome-adjacent variables rather than an adjustable confounder.

judge.rationale: The added columns perform a descriptive/correlational decomposition of the outcome: they flag which service subcategory scores are poor and label the weakest driver. This surfaces candidate causes/treatments (poor value-for-money, weakest category, per-category poor flags) but supplies ZERO confounders. A confounder here would be a common cause of both a subcategory rating and the recommendation that must be adjusted to avoid biased attribution -- e.g. Type of Traveller, Route, Month Flown, or reviewer disposition. None of these are added; nothing is surfaced from the data/text as a common cause. Worse, several columns (Overall Rating Band, and 'very_low_overall_rating' inside Non-Rec Risk Factors) are downstream proxies/mediators of the recommendation itself; treating them as explanatory factors would be a modelling mistake. Because the required treatment+confounder structure is absent (no common causes to adjust for), the causal-estimation claim is not realised. confounder_quality = 0.
